title: Viking Swords Had Steel Europe Couldn't Make for Centuries

scenes.text: Some Viking swords were made of steel Europe couldn't make for a thousand years.
They're stamped Ulfberht, and the best have about three times the carbon of normal medieval steel.
That needs crucible steel, melted hot enough to burn out impurities that made other blades brittle.
The Vikings likely imported it from Central Asia along the Volga trade route.
Europe made no crucible steel until the eighteenth century.

description:
Ulfberht swords, made around 800 to 1000 AD, used a high-carbon crucible steel that Europe would not produce itself until the 18th century.
Historians think the steel was imported along the Volga trade route from Central Asia.
What ancient technology amazes you most?
